title: Cooking in RKO theater dressing rooms because of segregated restaurants
summary: Because the band could not eat in white restaurants, they cooked backstage in the well-equipped RKO theater kitchens and dressing rooms.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Yeah. Oh, yeah. Do you remember the cooking? We used to cook -- ?
Sure. Well, you know why. The reason that you guys cooked is because we used to play a lot of towns in those days that you couldn't eat in white restaurants.
That's right, that's right.
I know the way we could get good food was to -- was we were cooking in the theater --
That's right.
Excuse me -- because in those days all the RKO theaters had beautiful back stages. They all had kitchens.
Sure did.
They had playrooms for the kids.
Sure.
Each dressing room had individual tables with your adjustable lights, chaise lounge, white sunken tub and bath for you to take a bath then if you wanted to.
Right.
Each room was named after a state.
Right.
And we all used to have -- we had so many rooms around there that --
Yeah.
The trombone section, we usually stay together, you know.
Yeah.
Sometimes when you all was cooking -- I know you and Tyree -- but you and Walter Thomas, oh, my --
Yes, well Tyree --

I never saw a room like that. Let me insert this. That room was chaos and when we got ready to leave Milt and Walter Thomas just take it like this, papers and everything, and say, 'Shrump,' shrump it up like that and put it in a bag.
We put them in whoever bag it was in.
That's right.
That's the truth, and (Unintelligible)
Then get it out.
sort it out when we got to the next town.
That's right.
"These your socks? These your shirts?" But it was still chaos in that room.
